title: UniSkill: Learning Actor-Aligned Skill Proposals for an Evolving Policy
title_zh: UniSkill: 学习演员对齐的技能提案以适应 evolving 策略

paragraphs.en: Large language model agents can improve across tasks by retaining reusable skills distilled from prior interactions. Recent work jointly optimizes task execution and skill extraction, enabling the policy and skillbank to co-evolve. However, as the actor continues learning, rewarding skill proposals through their reuse in subsequent training steps may conflate skill benefits with actor improvement, while directly testing each proposed skill requires costly additional actor rollouts. In this paper, we introduce UniSkill, which uses a shared policy to interact with the environment and propose skillbank edits ( Add , Update , or No Edit ) from the resulting trajectories. Specifically, the actor learns from environment rewards, while contrastive action feedback guides skill proposal learning. This feedback provides an actor-alignment signal by measuring how replacing the retrieved skill with a proposed skill changes the current actor’s action log-likelihood gap between previously collected successful and failed trajectories from the same task, thereby avoiding new rollouts for each proposal. Since proposal-level feedback may suppress an otherwise appropriate edit operation when the proposed skill content scores poorly, we further apply skill-edit support regularization to preserve exploration. Empirically, UniSkill achieves strong performance, reaching 98.4% success on ALFWorld and 84.7% on WebShop while maintaining stable joint training. Further ALFWorld experiments show that UniSkill remains effective when the shared policy uses a smaller backbone. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/LimOkii/UniSKill .

paragraphs.en: Existing approaches extract skills from interaction trajectories by prompting a powerful LLM with frozen parameters ( Ni et al., 2026 ; Xia et al., 2026 ) . Beyond fixed-model skill extraction, several methods jointly train the skill proposer and the actor ( Muhtar et al., 2026 ; Shi et al., 2026 ; Fan et al., 2026 ) . The actor interacts with the environment to complete tasks, and the resulting trajectories are used to extract skills that in turn guide subsequent interactions. As skill extraction becomes a learned capability, a central question is what learning feedback a newly proposed skill should receive. To provide this feedback, existing methods train models to generate reflections or extract skills using task-outcome prediction accuracy or rewards from the trajectories used for skill extraction ( Zhang et al., 2026b ; Shi et al., 2026 ) . These signals do not assess how the current actor would behave when given the proposed skill. More direct feedback can be obtained by evaluating task performance when the actor uses the skills in subsequent interactions ( Muhtar et al., 2026 ; He et al., 2026 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 现有方法通过用固定参数的强大 LLM 发出提示，从交互轨迹中提取技能（Ni et al., 2026；Xia et al., 2026）。 除了固定模型的技能提取方法外，还有几种方法会联合训练技能提出者和执行者（Muhtar et al., 2026；Shi et al., 2026；Fan et al., 2026）。 执行者与环境进行交互以完成任务，由此产生的轨迹被用于提取技能，而这些技能反过来又指导后续的交互。 随着技能提取成为一种可学习的能力，一个核心问题是：新提出的技能应该获得怎样的学习反馈？ 为了提供这种反馈，现有方法会训练模型生成反思或提取技能，其依据是任务结果预测的准确性，或是用于技能提取的轨迹所获得的奖励（Zhang et al., 2026b；Shi et al., 2026）。 这些信号并未评估当前执行者在获得所提出的技能后会如何行动。 通过评估执行者在后续交互中使用这些技能时的任务表现，可以获得更直接的反馈（Muhtar et al., 2026；He et al., 2026）。

paragraphs.en: However, the usefulness of a skill depends strongly on the actor that uses it ( Yu et al., 2026 ) . During joint training, the actor may already have been updated by the time the skill is reused. The updated actor might succeed even without the skill, so task success alone does not establish whether the skill would have helped the actor at the time it was proposed. Evaluating candidate skills before updating the actor avoids these intervening policy changes, but requires additional environment rollouts conditioned on each candidate skill, as in Evolving-RL ( Fan et al., 2026 ) . We therefore ask whether trajectories already collected by the current actor can provide learning feedback for new skill proposals.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，一项技能的有效性在很大程度上取决于使用该技能的智能体（Yu et al., 2026）。 在联合训练过程中，当技能被重新使用时，执行该动作的智能体可能已经过更新。 即使没有这项技能，更新后的智能体也可能成功，因此仅凭任务的成功并不能确定该技能在当时是否对智能体有所帮助。 在更新智能体之前评估候选技能可以避免这些中间策略的变化，但这需要针对每个候选技能进行额外的环境模拟，就像 Evolving-RL（Fan et al., 2026）中的做法一样。 因此，我们想知道当前智能体已经收集到的轨迹是否能为新提出的技能提供学习反馈。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we introduce UniSkill , a shared-policy framework that learns to act with retrieved skills and generate skill proposals from completed trajectories, as illustrated in Figure 2 . Each skill proposal specifies a skill-edit operation for adding a new skill, updating the retrieved skill, or leaving the skillbank unchanged. For Add and Update , the proposal also includes the corresponding new or revised skill content. To evaluate these proposed skills, we focus on actor alignment , the extent to which a proposed skill improves task performance for the current actor relative to the retrieved skill. We construct a proxy for this utility using previously collected successful and failed trajectories from the same task. Specifically, before the policy update, we hold the current actor and recorded behavior fixed and measure how replacing the retrieved skill with the proposed skill changes the action log-likelihood gap between these trajectories. We then combine this contrastive action feedback with rewards for the appropriateness of skill-edit operations to train the skill proposer, while the actor learns from environment rewards. Because the skill-edit operation and proposed content share a proposal-level training signal, negative feedback on the content may suppress an otherwise appropriate operation. We therefore use skill-edit support regularization to preserve exploration of these operations during joint training. Skill edits that pass both skill-critic and actor-alignment checks update the skillbank for subsequent interactions, allowing the policy and skillbank to co-evolve. As shown in Figure 1 , UniSkill achieves further gains in validation success during later training on ALFWorld, while continuing to add new skills and refine existing ones.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们介绍了 UniSkill——一种共享策略框架，它能够学习通过检索到的技能执行动作，并从已完成的任务轨迹中生成技能提案，如图 2 所示。 每个技能提案都指定了一项技能编辑操作：添加新技能、更新已检索的技能，或保持技能库不变。 对于“添加”和“更新”操作，提案还包括相应的新技能内容或修订后的技能内容。 为了评估这些拟议的技能，我们重点关注“执行者对齐度”，即拟议的技能相较于已检索的技能，在多大程度上能提升当前执行者的任务表现。 我们利用先前从同一任务中收集的成功和失败轨迹，构建了一个用于衡量这种效用的代理指标。 具体来说，在策略更新之前，我们保持当前执行者和记录的行为不变，并测量将已检索的技能替换为拟议的技能后，这些轨迹之间的动作对数似然度差距会发生怎样的变化。 随后，我们将这种对比性动作反馈与技能编辑操作适当性的奖励相结合，以训练技能提案生成器，而执行者则从环境奖励中学习。 由于技能编辑操作和拟议内容共享提案层面的训练信号，因此对内容的负面反馈可能会抑制原本适当的编辑操作。 因此，我们采用技能编辑支持正则化方法，在联合训练过程中保留对这些操作的探索。 通过技能评估器和执行者对齐度双重检验的技能编辑操作，会更新技能库以供后续交互使用，从而使得策略和技能库能够协同进化。 如图 1 所示，在 ALFWorld 的后期训练中，UniSkill 在验证成功率方面取得了进一步提升，同时持续添加新技能并优化现有技能。

paragraphs.zh: 我们通过对比当前智能体的动作对数似然度在先前收集的成功和失败轨迹上的表现，来比较所提议的技能与检索到的技能，从而开发对比性动作反馈，避免了每次提议都需要额外的模拟运行，并降低了技能评估的开销。

paragraphs.en: Prior work retains experience as verbal reflections and induced insights ( Shinn et al., 2023 ; Park et al., 2023 ; Zhao et al., 2024 ) , executable programs ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Zheng et al., 2025 ) , and abstracted workflows ( Wang et al., 2025b ) . A common approach prompts LLMs to extract and refine reusable guidance in external memory, without updating model parameters. For example, ReasoningBank prompts an LLM to extract reusable strategies from trajectories labeled as successful or failed by an LLM judge, storing them for subsequent retrieval ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) . Dynamic Cheatsheet uses a prompted curator to revise strategy memory ( Suzgun et al., 2026 ) , while ACE integrates extracted lessons into structured playbooks through incremental updates ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) . Beyond inference-time memory adaptation, EvolveR and SkillRL integrate experience reuse with policy optimization, refreshing stored principles or skills as training proceeds ( Wu et al., 2026 ; Xia et al., 2026 ) . SkillGraph models inter-skill dependencies to support structured retrieval and graph evolution during RL ( Li et al., 2026a ) . As policies and their stored experience co-evolve, a central question is how to evaluate and credit that experience for the current actor.
paragraphs.zh: 先前的研究将经验保留为语言性反思与归纳出的见解（Shinn 等，2023；Park 等，2023；Zhao 等，2024）、可执行的程序（Wang 等，2024；Zheng 等，2025）以及抽象化的工作流程（Wang 等，2025b）。 一种常见的方法是通过提示 LLM 从外部记忆中提取并提炼可重用的指导信息，而无需更新模型参数。 例如，ReasoningBank 会提示 LLM 从被 LLM 判官标记为成功或失败的轨迹中提取可重用的策略，并将其存储以便后续检索（Ouyang 等，2026）。 Dynamic Cheatsheet 使用受提示的策展人来修订策略记忆（Suzgun 等，2026），而 ACE 则通过增量更新将提取出的经验教训整合到结构化的操作手册中（Zhang 等，2026a）。 除了推理时的记忆适应外，EvolveR 和 SkillRL 还将经验复用与策略优化相结合，在训练过程中不断更新存储的原则或技能（Wu 等，2026；Xia 等，2026）。 SkillGraph 对技能间的依赖关系进行建模，以支持在强化学习过程中的结构化检索与图结构演化（Li 等，2026a）。 随着策略及其存储的经验共同演化，一个核心问题是如何评估这种经验，并将其成果归因于当前的执行者。

paragraphs.en: RetroAgent rewards correct task-outcome predictions during reflection ( Zhang et al., 2026b ) , while Skill1 rewards skill distillation using task returns relative to the highest historical utility among retrieved skills ( Shi et al., 2026 ) . These rewards guide skill generation, but do not directly evaluate whether the generated skill helps the actor. Learning feedback for skill generation and use can instead depend on whether the actor completes a task successfully using skills ( Wang et al., 2025a ; Li et al., 2026b ) . Complementary RL trains its skill proposer from outcomes of later skill reuse ( Muhtar et al., 2026 ) , while ReSkill compares skillbank revisions across training steps and discounts older outcomes ( He et al., 2026 ) . MASA demonstrates that skill effectiveness varies across model backbones, highlighting the need for actor-specific skill evaluation ( Yu et al., 2026 ) . During joint training, by the time a proposed skill is used and evaluated on a subsequent task, the actor may already have been updated. Evolving-RL evaluates candidate skills before the joint policy update through additional skill-conditioned rollouts ( Fan et al., 2026 ) . UniSkill instead holds the current actor and recorded trajectories fixed, comparing action likelihoods under the retrieved and proposed skills to train the skill proposer without additional evaluation rollouts.
paragraphs.zh: RetroAgent 在反思阶段奖励对任务结果的准确预测（Zhang et al., 2026b），而 Skill1 则通过比较任务回报与检索到的技能中历史最高效用之间的差异来奖励技能蒸馏（Shi et al., 2026）。 这些奖励机制指导了技能的生成，但并未直接评估所生成的技能是否有助于执行者。 技能生成与使用的学习反馈可以转而取决于执行者是否成功利用技能完成了任务（Wang et al., 2025a；Li et al., 2026b）。 Complementary RL 通过后续技能重用的结果训练其技能提议器（Muhtar et al., 2026），而 ReSkill 则跨训练步骤比较技能库的修订版本，并对较旧的结果进行折扣处理（He et al., 2026）。 MASA 表明，技能的有效性会因模型基础架构的不同而有所差异，这凸显了针对特定执行者进行技能评估的必要性（Yu et al., 2026）。 在联合训练过程中，当某个提议的技能被用于后续任务并接受评估时，执行者可能已经过更新。 Evolving-RL 通过额外的技能条件化展开，在联合策略更新之前对候选技能进行评估（Fan et al., 2026）。 UniSkill 则保持当前执行者和已记录轨迹不变，通过比较在检索到的技能和提议的技能下动作的可能性来训练技能提议器，而无需额外的评估展开。

sents.en: After the policy update, we apply Add and Update proposals that pass both critic checks and satisfy Δ + > 0 \Delta^{+}>0 and R align > 0 R_{\mathrm{align}}>0 .

paragraphs.en: Table 2 shows that UniSkill retains 96.1% success when skill retrieval is disabled at evaluation, compared with 84.4% for both Actor Only and the variant without the R align R_{\mathrm{align}} reward, and 34.4% for Skill Proposer Only. paragraphs.en: We present UniSkill, which jointly learns task execution and skill proposals with a shared policy, enabling the actor and skillbank to co-evolve. Actor-aligned feedback from previously collected trajectories reduces skill-evaluation overhead, while support regularization sustains exploration across skill-edit operations throughout training. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop demonstrate strong task performance and stable joint training. Further ALFWorld experiments show that UniSkill remains effective when the shared policy uses a smaller backbone.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 UniSkill，它通过共享策略联合学习任务执行与技能提案，使智能体与技能库能够协同进化。 来自先前收集轨迹的、与智能体对齐的反馈降低了技能评估的开销，而支持正则化则在训练全程维持了跨技能编辑操作的探索能力。 在 ALFWorld 和 WebShop 上的实验表明，该方法具有强大的任务执行能力和稳定的联合训练表现。 进一步的 ALFWorld 实验显示，即使共享策略使用较小的主干网络，UniSkill 仍然有效。

paragraphs.en: We organize the cases from two complementary viewpoints. First, we follow committed skills across training to show how interaction evidence produces Add and Update operations and how the resulting guidance is later reused. Second, we use the Q2 protocol to isolate the immediate effect of a candidate skill: the task and actor checkpoint are fixed, and only the directly supplied skill condition changes. The fixed-actor cases include cases in which R align R_{\mathrm{align}} and rollout utility agree, covering both positive-positive and negative-negative outcomes, as well as diagnostic cases in which positive alignment does not yield a positive rollout gain. We report raw R align R_{\mathrm{align}} unless clipping is stated.
paragraphs.zh: 我们从两个互补的视角来组织这些案例。 首先，我们追踪训练过程中已承诺的技能，以展示交互证据如何产生“添加”和“更新”操作，以及由此产生的指导如何被后续复用。 其次，我们使用 Q2 协议来隔离候选技能的即时影响：任务和执行者检查点是固定的，只有直接提供的技能条件会发生变化。 固定执行者的案例包括 R 与 R_{\mathrm{align}} 一致且展开效用相符的案例，涵盖正-正和负-负结果，也包括诊断性案例，即正向对齐并未带来正向的展开增益。 除非另有说明进行了截断处理，否则我们报告原始的 R align R_{\mathrm{align}}。

paragraphs.en: Together, the cases separate three sources of disagreement.
